A decade after Britain voted to leave the European Union, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has sealed a reset deal with Brussels covering food and farm trade, a link between carbon markets and a youth mobility scheme for 100,000 young people from each side. Burnham says the package could add up to 0.5% to the U.K. economy, and he has said he would like to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime.
So what exactly has been agreed, what is Britain giving up in return, and is the country really preparing to undo Brexit?
